name: Low-tier routing for test-only beads
hypothesis: Beads matching IsTestOnlyBead() (title starts with 'Add tests for'/'Write tests for') succeed on the low tier (haiku for Claude, gpt-5.3-codex-spark for Codex) at >=85% first-pass rate, reducing cost from ~$1.07-$2.13 to ~$0.25-$0.47 per test bead
change: In SelectTier() and process.go setupBeadContext, return low tier for beads where bead.IsTestOnlyBead() returns true, unless the bead has a complexity label override. This routes to haiku or codex-spark based on the existing provider routing ratio (claude:1, openai:99)
measurement: Track success rate and cost of test-only beads on low tier over 20 iterations. Success threshold: >=85% first-pass success rate. Cost threshold: >=40% reduction vs medium-tier baseline for test beads
risk: Test-only beads may still require understanding complex package internals. Lower-tier models may produce tests that compile but don't meaningfully cover behavior. Mitigation: validation phase catches compilation failures; review phase catches weak tests; escalation chain promotes to medium/high on failure
